queue.title: This Week in Canada: Breaking Up Is Hard to Do
queue.dek: In the latest This Week in Canada newsletter: Alberta’s separatism vote went down to defeat, but the overtaxation, overregulation, and other grievances that fueled the movement are as entrenched as ever, writes Rupa Subramanya.
queue.opening: Welcome back to This Week in Canada, where Monday’s defeat of the separatism referendum in Alberta isn’t anywhere close to the end of the forces that put the question on the ballot. Let’s jump right in! The most serious challenge to Canada’s national unity in more than three decades is officially over. Alberta isn’t going anywhere. But that doesn’t change the fact that separatists got this far over something that was considered a fringe cause until recently. And the story of how they did it is about much more than Alberta separatism. It’s about a deeper disillusionment among Canadian conservatives—and why some of them still see Alberta as a refuge from a country that they no longer recognize. First, the numbers. Results as of early Tuesday morning showed about 76 percent in favor of remaining in Canada and 24 percent supporting a binding vote on whether to leave.
